searchText: P2P don't hash over the compressed form. It's uncompressed before it's decoded. true but does that mean that the go snappy lib will happily decompress the java libs form (if hypothetically, it doesnt match its own)? Yes. It has a non-deterministic encoding but a deterministic decoding. Even if the algorithms produced the same encoding, if an alternate but legal encoding exists (even if less-efficient) it shouldn't be hashed over. got it, thanks i guess we'll have to hash the decompressed value These sorts of malleability attacks caused (still cause?) problems in bitcoin.
